newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan needs 5 years to re-enter Japan pork market.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan needs 5 years to re-enter Japan pork market.

text.p: A Council of Agriculture official said on Tuesday that Taiwan, struggling to halt an outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease, had little chance of resuming pork exports to Japan within five years.
"It will be difficult to resume pork exports to Japan within five years," Chyr Shuang-ching, a senior official in the cabinet-level council, told Reuters by telephone.

The council banned all fresh and frozen pork exports on March 20 after confirming an outbreak of the deadly contagion on feedlots across Taiwan, sending the huge hog industry into crisis with massive slaughtering ordered islandwide.
Japan and South Korea, the main foreign markets for the island's pork, responded by banning pork imports from Taiwan to protect their own herds.
The farm council issued new figures on Monday showing the magnitude of the crisis, saying the disease had been detected at 357 breeding centers -- up from just nine on March 20.
The council ordered the slaughter of all hogs, even healthy ones, at affected farms to ensure total eradication of the disease and said this meant 389,171 hogs would be destroyed.
